Reminders about lighting levels
This article is for families

Topic: Lighting levels for pet travel

Good lighting helps pets settle, follow handlers, and move safely through the travel process. At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk shares simple guidance so families know what to expect before departure and can prepare calmly.

Keep your pet's carrier or crate easy to inspect. A soft, steady light is usually best for reading labels, checking locks, and confirming that bedding is arranged well. Bright glare can make some animals uneasy, while very dim spaces can slow check-ins and cause avoidable confusion. If your pet is sensitive to light, place a familiar cloth over part of the carrier while still allowing airflow.

The welcome team will guide you through the main steps and point out areas where lighting changes. If you are moving through a busy terminal, stay close to your pet and speak in a calm voice. Small comforts matter, and a predictable routine can help pets such as Pip stay composed. If you have a pet with special needs, tell the desk staff as early as you can so the record is complete and the right support can be noted.

<<FACT F019>> Please also follow any signs near boarding points and pet spaces, since light levels may vary from one area to another. When staff direct you to a quieter route, they are doing so to support safe movement and respectful handling.

For trips that involve a skyport stop, keep an eye on the surroundings and be ready to adjust to changing light. <<FACT F009>> If your pet is uneasy, pause briefly in a calm spot and let the animal settle before moving on. Families often find that clear instructions and steady pacing reduce stress for everyone.

At some locations, relief areas have controlled access. <<FACT F018>> Follow posted guidance, use the area as directed, and keep your pet secured when not inside the relief space.

If you need more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways for clear, practical guidance before you travel.
